Prioritize Workers & Pages for all new applications. Use the official `wrangler` CLI for scaffolding and deployment. Always start with `wrangler generate`.
npx wrangler generate my-worker --type=module --ts
npx create-cloudflare@latest my-fullstack-app --framework next

For multiple apps, use `pnpm` or `yarn workspaces`; centralize dependencies/build scripts (`"workspaces": ["apps/*", "packages/*"]`).

Manage secrets securely via `wrangler.toml` or the Cloudflare dashboard. Use `.dev.vars` for local development. Storing sensitive data directly in code or `.env` files that aren't `.dev.vars`. Use `.dev.vars` for local secrets, and integrate with CLI tools.
dotenv -e .dev.vars -- npx prisma migrate dev
Keep `wrangler.toml`, `.dev.vars`, and `DATABASE_URL` available as appropriate.

Design for the edge: stateless Workers, stateful Durable Objects. Workers are stateless and globally distributed. Avoid in-memory state that needs to persist across requests or instances. Relying on global variables for user sessions or shared data. Use KV for simple key-value storage, D1 for relational data, or Durable Objects for strong consistency and real-time state. Use D1 for new, natively serverless relational databases; use Hyperdrive for edge acceleration to existing regional databases.

Always use R2 for large file storage. Benefit from zero egress fees and global distribution. Securely expose internal services without opening firewall ports. Integrate SSO for private apps. Use `cloudflared` for secure access to Azure, AWS, GCP, or on-prem resources.
cloudflared tunnel create Azure-01

Keep Worker bundles as small as possible. Tree-shake dependencies aggressively. Importing large, unoptimized libraries. Use `esbuild` and minimal imports. For Prisma, use `engineType: "client"` and an edge-compatible driver adapter; avoid Rust binaries. Configure `schema.prisma`; use Prisma Accelerate if needed. Relevant paths: `src/index.ts`, `<REDACTED_USER>/client/edge`, `<REDACTED_USER>/extension-accelerate`.

Leverage Cloudflare CDN caching for static assets and API responses; set appropriate `Cache-Control` headers. Workers are single-threaded, event-driven, and have no Node.js APIs. All I/O operations *must* be `await`ed. Synchronous file system operations or long-running CPU-bound tasks. Use asynchronous network, KV, and D1 operations.

Always configure WAF, Bot Fight Mode, and Rate Limiting. Deploying public APIs without edge security. Implement granular rate limiting for login endpoints, API abuse, and `cf_clearance` cookie reuse.

Test early, test often, and test at the edge. Use Vitest or Jest for unit tests; Miniflare for local Workers runtime/bindings testing (KV, D1, R2); Playwright or Cypress for end-to-end tests. Test paths: `my-logic.test.ts`, `worker.test.ts`, `dist/index.mjs`.
npx wrangler deploy --env staging
npx playwright test --project=staging
